text: One is led by the passage in Genesis 22 to read the three days of travel as a kind of suspended sentence; for during them nothing outwardly happens, while all that signifies is in fact happening. The emphasis falls on the servants, the wood, the knife, and the fire, so that the instruments of the act are named before the act itself has come. Obedience and horror remain joined in the story, with neither suffered to prevail over the other. Faith in this story has no character of feeling; it is ordered in fixed relations, like a geometry, among the servants, the wood, the knife, and the fire.
